name: OH-12
label: Likely R

key_factors: District partisan lean of R+15 gives Republicans a deep structural advantage
Balderson's fundraising dominance: $2.1M raised vs. Christian's $131K
Prediction markets price a Democratic upset at only about 4-5%
No public polling; the national environment favors Democrats but only trims the margin
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Balderson's incumbency, and his roughly sixteen-to-one fundraising edge leave Christian with a very narrow path, and markets agree in pricing the upset near four percent. The favorable national environment shaves a couple of points off the expected margin but nowhere near enough to matter.
model.watch: A wave of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected incumbent scandal could widen the race, but no such signs have appeared.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Troy Balderson seeks another term in a central Ohio district whose partisan lean runs about fifteen points toward the GOP. That structural advantage, paired with incumbency, presents a steep obstacle for Democratic challenger Jerrad Christian. No public general-election polls are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, campaign money, and market pricing.

Fundraising shows a wide gap: Balderson has raised about $2.1 million and holds roughly $1.1 million on hand, while Christian has brought in about $131,000 with some $24,000 available. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a four percent chance of an upset. The national environment favors Democrats this cycle, which trims the expected Republican margin modestly but does not come close to closing a gap of this size.
